prompt_text: I need a personal injury lawyer in Denver after a car accident. Which specific law firms should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Denver for a car accident case?
answer_verbatim:
I can point you to specific firms, but first it will help to know a few details so I can tailor recommendations: how badly were you injured (minor, moderate, severe/permanent)? Do you prefer a large firm with lots of resources or a smaller boutique that will personally handle your case? Do you want someone who will go to trial if necessary? Which Denver neighborhood or ZIP code are you in (so I can suggest firms that commonly handle cases in your county)?

If you want names right away, I can give a short list of the kinds of firms you should call and why — but because I can’t browse the web from here, the best results come if you tell me the details above so I can tailor the list and the questions to ask.

Meanwhile, here’s practical guidance you can use immediately — who to call, what to ask, and why those factors matter:

Who to call (types of firms)
- Local plaintiff-only personal injury firms in Denver — these focus on representing people (not insurers) and usually handle car-accident injury claims from start to finish.
- Mid-size plaintiff firms with trial experience — they have resources for medical experts and litigation if the insurer refuses to settle.
- Boutique catastrophic-injury firms — if your injuries are severe or permanent, call a firm that specializes in catastrophic injury and life-care planning.
- Firms that offer a free consultation and contingency-fee arrangements (they only get paid if you recover money).

Why these matter
- Plaintiff-only = no conflicts of interest with insurers.
- Trial experience = leverage in settlement negotiations.
- Resources = ability to obtain medical experts, accident reconstruction, and to advance case expenses.
- Contingency fee and clear fee structure protect you from up-front costs.

Questions to ask on the first call
1. Do you handle car-accident personal injury cases, and what percentage of your practice is plaintiff-side car crashes? (Look for firms heavily focused on plaintiff PI.)
2. How many car accident cases have you taken to trial in the past 5 years? (Trial experience matters.)
3. Who will handle my case day-to-day — the lead attorney or a paralegal/junior associate? Can I meet the lead attorney? (You want to know who you’ll deal with.)
4. What is your fee structure and contingency percentage? Are there any additional costs I’ll be responsible for? (Ask about medical lien handling and subrogation.)
5. Do you have experience with my type of injury (e.g., neck/back, orthopedic surgery, TBI, spinal cord)? (Specialized experience helps value cases.)
6. Do you offer a free consultation and, if hired, will you take the case on contingency? (Most reputable PI firms do.)
7. What results have you obtained for similar cases? (Ask for representative settlements/verdicts — not guarantees but a sense of track record.)
8. How do you communicate with clients? (frequency, email/text, online portal)

What to bring to a consultation or have ready on the call
- Crash report / police report number
- Photos of the scene and vehicle damage
- Names/contacts of witnesses
- Your medical records and bills or at least the names of treating providers
- Your insurance information (your policy and any communications)
- Date/time/location of accident

Red flags to avoid
- Firms that ask for upfront “retainer” payments for a typical car accident (most work contingency).
- Vague answers about who will handle your case or guaranteed outcomes.
- Large advertising-only firms that outsource most work — you want to meet the actual lawyer.

How many firms to contact
- Call at least 3 law firms for free consultations, compare responses on experience, communication style, and fee structure, then pick the best fit.

Next step I can do for you
- If you tell me: (1) the severity of your injuries, (2) whether you want trial-ready counsel or just a negotiator, and (3) your Denver ZIP or neighborhood, I’ll produce a short, specific list of 6–8 Denver plaintiff personal-injury law firms that match your needs and why to call each one — plus a short phone script you can use on the first call.

Tell me those 3 details and I’ll create the tailored list and script.
